bots.name: Freqtrade
bots.exit: Exit signals + ROI table + stoploss + trailing stop
bots.position_sizing: Fixed stake, available balance fractions, or custom callbacks
bots.risk_management: Stoploss, max open trades, protection plugins (cooldown, etc.)
bots.execution: CCXT exchange API; dry-run and live modes
bots.data: OHLCV from exchanges; optional informative pairs
bots.backtest_notes: Built-in backtester; results highly strategy-specific; easy to overfit hyperopt
bots.limitations: No universal edge; hyperopt overfitting risk; exchange fees/slippage often underestimated
bots.inspection_summary: Core loop loads OHLCV, computes indicators in user strategy, generates entries/exits, applies ROI/stoploss, sizes stakes, and routes orders via CCXT. Hyperopt optimizes parameters against backtest metrics — a major overfitting vector if abused.

bots.name: Hummingbot
bots.signals: Fair value mid; inventory skew; optional Avellaneda-Stoikov reservation price
bots.entry: Post bid/ask around reservation price / spreads
bots.exit: Inventory-targeted quote adjustments; optional hanging order logic
bots.risk_management: Inventory band, kill switches, exchange circuit patterns
bots.execution: Connector architecture to CEX/DEX; websocket order books
bots.backtest_notes: Strategy backtesting support exists but MM backtests are microstructure-sensitive
bots.limitations: Adverse selection vs professionals; latency; toxic flow on some venues
bots.inspection_summary: Strategy modules compute reservation prices and optimal spreads (Avellaneda-Stoikov variant), maintain inventory targets, and manage two-sided quotes through exchange connectors.

bots.name: Jesse
bots.backtest_notes: Research-oriented backtester with metrics reporting
bots.limitations: Edge depends entirely on user strategy quality
bots.inspection_summary: UNKNOWN — framework inspected at documentation level only in this release

bots.name: OctoBot
bots.backtest_notes: Supports backtesting via tentacles
bots.limitations: Complex plugin surface; strategy quality varies

bots.name: Gekko (archived lineage)
bots.backtest_notes: Popular historically; many public strategies are overfit toy examples
bots.limitations: Archived; educational more than production edge
bots.inspection_summary: Historical reference system; treat public strategy posts as weak evidence

bots.name: Zenbot
bots.signals: Built-in strategies (trend following, mean reversion variants)
bots.backtest_notes: Simulated trades; not a verified live edge
bots.limitations: Maintenance uneven; no verified alpha claim

bots.name: NautilusTrader
bots.backtest_notes: High-fidelity backtesting focus — better microstructure realism than toy bots
bots.limitations: Framework, not a strategy; edge still user-supplied
bots.inspection_summary: Event-driven engine with cache, data, execution, and risk components; designed for research-to-live parity rather than shipping a single profitable strategy.

bots.name: hftbacktest
bots.data: Full order book / trade feeds for backtest
bots.backtest_notes: Research tool for HFT MM; does not provide a production edge by itself
bots.limitations: Requires expensive data; strategy still proprietary to researcher
bots.inspection_summary: Provides queue-based market replay and inventory-aware MM examples; useful for testing latency/queue assumptions, not a turnkey alpha product.

bots.name: FinRL
bots.signals: Learned RL policy over market state features
bots.risk_management: Environment-level constraints in examples; often insufficient vs real trading
bots.execution: Usually abstracted fills in research envs
bots.backtest_notes: Research benchmarks; published metrics often ignore realistic costs/slippage regimes
bots.limitations: Overfitting, non-stationarity, unrealistic execution — place in weak-evidence watchlist unless carefully validated
bots.inspection_summary: Builds OpenAI-Gym-style market environments and trains DRL agents (A2C/PPO/etc.). Example pipelines emphasize research reproducibility more than live microstructure realism.

bots.name: Microsoft Qlib
bots.signals: ML models (LightGBM, Transformer variants, etc.) on alpha factors
bots.entry: Top-k / drop-out portfolio from prediction scores
bots.risk_management: Limiters / cost models available in workflow
bots.backtest_notes: Strong research workflow; published example metrics are not live fund returns
bots.limitations: Alpha decay; data snooping if feature libraries searched aggressively
bots.inspection_summary: End-to-end quant research platform: data layer, operators, models, portfolio generation, and backtest. Useful reference for industrial ML quant workflows.

bots.name: VectorBT
bots.backtest_notes: Extremely fast research; can accelerate overfitting if abused

bots.name: Backtrader
bots.execution: Brokers simulated; some live integrations community-maintained
bots.backtest_notes: Classic retail research framework
bots.limitations: Strategy-dependent; many public examples ignore costs

bots.name: Zipline / Zipline-Reloaded
bots.backtest_notes: Quantopian lineage; educational factor workflows
bots.inspection_summary: Pipeline API computes point-in-time factors; algorithm API rebalances to target weights with commission/slippage models — good for factor research hygiene.

bots.name: QuantConnect Lean
bots.execution: Brokerage models; live deployments on QC cloud
bots.backtest_notes: Professional-grade research engine used by many public shared algorithms
bots.limitations: Public shared algos vary wildly in quality; treat as unverified
bots.inspection_summary: Event-driven algorithm framework with data feeds, scheduling, portfolio, and brokerage abstractions; hosts many community strategies of uneven evidence quality.

bots.inspection_summary: Companion RL library to FinRL ecosystem
